Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City
Council must disclose any campaign contribution over $250 (aggregated) within the preceding 12 months made by the party, their
agent, and those required to be aggregated with their contributions under Gov. Code § 82015.5. The disclosure must include the
amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to
these regulations.

  REGULAR MEETING

Mayor Rios called the meeting to order 6:09 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to roll call were
Councilmembers Perez, Ramirez, and Valencia, Vice Mayor Ayala, and Mayor Rios.
Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Arnold M. Alvarez, City Attorney;
and Theresa Devoy, City Clerk.

The invocation was delivered by Soomin Kim, Korean Seventh-Day Adventist Church;
followed by the flag salute, led by Rosalie Ramirez, New Harvest Christian School.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

City Council wished all mothers a Happy Mother’s Day. Councilmember Perez shared
that City newsletters were distributed and encouraged all to participate in the various
activities and events; reported on her attendance at Scholas United States of America
Foundation event; and encouraged students to finish the school year strong.
Councilmember Valencia reported on her attendance at the City of Bell’s Swearing in
Ceremony, Thinkers 4 Autism 6th Annual Autism Awareness Fair, Robert “Bob” White
Park Ribbon Cutting Ceremony, funeral services for former Commissioner Martin
Greenidge, and Sunday brunch at El Baja Bar and Grill; and requested the meeting be
adjourned in memory of Martin Greenidge. Mayor Rios reported on her attendance at
the Pelota De Trapo event, the Cerritos Military Ball, Robert “Bob” White Park Ribbon
Cutting Ceremony, and the Meet the Mayor event; reminded residents to be responsible
pet owners; and shared that El Baja Bar and Grill was featured in the local news.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council presented a proclamation declaring May 5 - May 11, 2024 as Municipal
Clerk’s Week in the City of Norwalk.

City Council presented a proclamation declaring May as Older Americans Month in the
City of Norwalk.

City Council presented a proclamation declaring May 8, 2024, as California Day of the
Teacher.

City Council presented a proclamation declaring May 19 – May 25, 2024 as Classified
School Employee Week in the City of Norwalk.

SUBJECT:  SOFTWARE AGREEMENT  FOR  ACCOUNTING  STANDARDS  BOARD
  COMPLIANCE

Background:

In May of 2020, the Government Accounting Standards Board (“GASB”) released Statement No.
96 which provides guidance on the accounting and financial reporting requirements for
government end-users of subscription-based information technology arrangements (“SBITAs”)
which consists of all software licenses and subscriptions. GASB 96 serves as an extension of
existing reporting requirements under GASB 87, which requires public entities to report on all
leases. GASB 96 went into effect, June 15, 2022, which required the City to monitor, record and
report on all software purchases as part of the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for Fiscal
Year 2022-2023.

To ensure compliance with existing, new and any forthcoming GASB requirements, in early 2023
City staff conducted a search for technology-based solutions available in the market that
specialize in government entity financial reporting requirements. Following thorough reviews,
demonstrations and negotiations with various firms, the City determined that the DebtBook
system best met the current and foreseeable needs of the City.

Following the first year of implementation and use, the City has successfully completed
necessary reporting and continued monitoring over its leases, software and debt; all of which
have now been consolidated into one easy-to-use platform resulting in streamlined reporting and
accessibility of necessary documents, reports and records.

Analysis:

The City entered into an annual software agreement with Debtbook that is set to expire May 30,
2024. The City has two options to renew the software subscription to avoid disruption in
monitoring:
 City Council  May 28, 2024
Approval of Software Agreement  Page No. 2

Option 1:
  • Enter into a three-year agreement with DebtBook, that provides a discounted annual
  subscription fee, for a total contract value of $66,300 over the term of the agreement and
  fixed pricing as follows:

  Year  Period  Subscription Fee
  Year 1  June 1, 2024, through May 30, 2025  $21,000
  Year 2  June 1, 2025, through May 30, 2026  $22,100
  Year 3  June 1, 2026, through May 30, 2027  $23,200
  TOTAL  $66,300

Option 2:
  • Enter into another one-year agreement in the amount of $23,000, that is within the City
  Manager’s signing authority to continue services.

DebtBook utilizes a tiered fee schedule that is dictated by the number of records stored in the
system annually. As such, the total annual subscription cost of the system can vary as the City
continues to purchase software and subscriptions and enters into new leases.

By entering into a three-year agreement with DebtBook, the City has an annual fixed subscription
for three years that will not be adjusted based on the number of records. Additionally, by entering
into a three-year agreement, rather than a one-year agreement, the City receives discounted
annual rates that would not otherwise be offered by simply renewing the subscription on a year-
to-year basis.

To take advantage of discounted pricing, and fixed subscription fees, staff recommends
renewing through Option 1 by entering into a three-year agreement with DebtBook which will
result in long-term savings for the City to continue its required monitoring and reporting for GASB
compliance.

Fiscal Impact:

The cost of the DebtBook software subscription is currently budgeted in the current fiscal year.
Years two and three costs will be included as part of the City’s regular budget process.

Background:

The City of Norwalk, as the lead agency under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
is proposing Capital Improvement Project No. 7607 – Stormwater Capture and Infiltration
Project.

The City has received Measure W Funds for the stormwater capture and infiltration project
(Project) from the Lower San Gabriel River Watershed Management Program (LSGR WMP)
Group. The project will capture dry-weather flows at two locations. The first location is an
existing storm drain on Horst Avenue adjacent to the park. The second location is within the
park from an existing Los Angeles County Flood Control District storm drain culvert. Up to 50
cubic feet per second (cfs) of combined dry weather flows from both the storm drain and storm
drain culvert will be diverted and stored in underground infiltration gallery/detention basins. The
underground basins provide storage for up to 11.8 acre-feet of flow, approximately the size of
six Olympic size swimming pools. These improvements are to be constructed in the northern
half of the park, and includes the appurtenant diversion piping, pumps, and a treatment system
to supply recycled water for onsite irrigation.

The City has also received Proposition 68 Funds for the rehabilitation of Hermosillo Park
(PROJECT) from the LSGR WMP Group. The project will rehabilitate Hermosillo Park in its
entirety which includes the construction of a new reception building, new turf grass, irrigation,
landscaping, hardscape, parking lot, playground area, basketball courts, soccer and multi-use
fields and lighting for the fields.

Background:

The City’s Strategic Plan outlines the City’s commitment to sustainability and climate
resistance. To do so, staff worked with Syserco Energy Solutions (“SES”), a qualified
energy services company, to develop an analysis of opportunities for the City to upgrade
its facilities to achieve energy efficiency and cost savings measures for the City.

Necessary energy conservation measures identified included:

  •  Installation of solar panel arrays at several facilities
  •  Installation of energy efficient “cool” roofs at the City’s Transportation Center/Public
  Services facility buildings
  •  Installation of building management system thermostats at several facilities
  •  Retrofitting ballfield lighting at two City parks
  •  Installation of ballfield lighting at several parks
  •  Replacement of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning control (HVAC) units older
  than 18 years
  •  Refurbishment of HVAC units to provide protective polyurethane coating
  •  Replacement of transformers at City Hall to a high efficiency unit
  •  Building exterior upgrades to add/replace door sweeps and sealing doors

Solar Energy Project Lease Financing

On November 7, 2023, City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-68 authorizing the City
Manager to finalize negotiations with SES and acquire the necessary conservation
equipment to implement the energy conservation measures through the Sustainability,
Energy Efficiency Infrastructure Improvement Project. The City Council also authorized
the City Manager to secure necessary financing for the solar panel installation component
of the project (“Project”). On February 6, 2024, City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-
08 engaging a finance team for the financing of the Project that covers six locations and
has been divided into two separate projects as follows: City Hall, Transit Center and
Social Services facilities do not qualify for Low Income Credit (LIC) and are collectively
known as the Non-LIC Facilities Project with cost of $7,000,000; Sports Complex, Aquatic
Pavilion and Well 10 facilities do qualify for LIC and are collectively known as LIC Facilities
Project with a cost of $5,000,000.

The total cost of both projects is $12,400,000, including a $450,000 contingency. Of this
amount, the City will finance $5,000,000 of Non-LIC Facilities Project and advance
approximately $3.8 million in anticipated rebates from the Building Renovation Fund to
fund LIC Facilities Project. The rebates are expected to be received and replenish the
Building Renovation Fund once the installation of the Project is complete in two years.
The balance of the costs are allocated to the Proposition C Fund and the Water Fund,
due to the location and use of facilities where the solar panels are to be installed.

The City, with assistance of its Municipal Advisor, determined that a private placement
(that is, direct financing with one lender) would be quicker and more cost effective than a
stand-alone bond issuance to fund the $5,000,000. Timing was an important factor, since
certain rebates available to the City will be reduced if the Project doesn’t commence by
December 31, 2024. The staff will provide SES with a notice to proceed on the Project
as soon as the financing is in hand.

The Underwriter, acting as a Placement Agent, solicited bids to provide financing from
seven lenders. The best bid was received from Webster Bank, National Association
(“Webster Bank”), at a rate of 4.44% for 15 years.

The next step in the process is to approve the form of various agreements in connection
with the financing. Resolution No. 24-21authorizes the following documents:

  •  Lease Agreement by and between the City and Webster Bank setting out the terms
  and conditions of the funding of the Project and terms for repayment;
  •  Purchaser Letter (Exhibit D to Lease Agreement) by Webster Bank containing
  certain representations;
  •  Escrow Agreement by and among the City, Webster Bank and US Bank, setting
  out the terms under which the funds for construction will be administered during
  the construction period; and

Resolution No. 24-21 authorizes (1) the Lease Agreement to be executed in an amount
not in excess of $5,500,000, (2) the City Manager to sign a “rate lock letter” with Webster
Bank locking in the 4.44% proposed interest rate until the closing date of June 12, 2024
and (3) the City Manager and the Director of Finance to execute the documents as
necessary in connection with the financing.

Fiscal Impact:

The City expects that the Lease Agreement will be executed in the principal amount of
$5,458,000. This will fund $5,000,000 in Non-LIC Facilities Project Costs, $117,000 in
costs of issuance and $341,000 in capitalized interest. The Capitalized Interest Funds
will be used to pay interest on the Lease Agreement during the construction period, and
before the City is receiving the benefit of the lower energy costs resulting from the
installation of the solar panels.

Interest on the Lease Agreement through December 1, 2025 will be paid from the
Capitalized Interest Funds. The annual lease payments will be $532,000 for 14 years
commencing in Fiscal Year 2026/27, with an interest-only lease payment of $121,000 in
Fiscal Year 2025/26.

The costs of issuance include bond counsel fees, special tax counsel fees, municipal
advisor fees and placement agent fees, payable under agreements approved by
Resolution No. 24-08.
